notes: Large-source-unit review: both flagged units are `לְ` + `בַד` + `מִן` → *besides*. Each morpheme was accounted against the rendering — one English word stands for the whole compound preposition, no morpheme owns a part of it, and the subtraction test leaves all three without any rendering when it is dropped — so rule 30's one-rendering condition is met and the groupings are retained, headed on `בַד`, the morpheme carrying the lexeme.
The italic *shekels* is `added` as a measure noun the Hebrew never writes (rules 7, 33), while *of gold* is the appositional measure nominal's own supplied preposition.
In *the golden ear rings* and *the purple raiment* the written *the* stands before the attributive's own word, which is where the article morpheme sits, so the article takes it (rule 29).
